observations: Photo 0 shows a used electric dry pressing iron (no visible water tank).

claims.claim: A used dry pressing iron that is still working is available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show it being switched on or any test result; only the iron and cord are visible.

risks.risk: The iron may not heat properly (thermostat/heating element fault).
risks.proof: A short video of the iron plugged in and switched on, showing it heating (e.g., temperature rise on the soleplate or steam/heat behavior if applicable).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not working / needs repair.

risks.risk: Electrical safety risk due to visible cord/plug wear or damage near the plug end.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the plug pins and the entire cord length, plus a test showing no sparking/overheating when plugged in.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as unsafe/needs cord replacement.

risks.risk: Soleplate condition may be poor (stains, scratches, or residue) affecting ironing quality.
risks.proof: Photo of the soleplate straight-on in good light, and a quick ironing test on a scrap cloth.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as cosmetically worn and ironing performance not guaranteed.

proof_requests: Send a video: plug in, switch on, and show the soleplate heating for at least 2–3 minutes.
Send close-up photos of the plug and the cord damage area (both sides), and confirm if the cord has been repaired.
Show the temperature control/dial (if any) and a quick ironing test on a small piece of fabric.
response.reason: The seller says it is working, but the photo only shows a dry iron with visible cord/plug wear and no proof of heating. Without a working test, the worst-case (not working/unsafe) pricing applies, so we need proof first.
